outputs.L3: This work establishes a duality theorem for a class of graded algebras, providing a framework for relating their algebraic and cohomological properties. It then applies this perspective to the study of local cohomology, with particular emphasis on tameness—that is, the eventual pattern of vanishing or nonvanishing among the graded components of local cohomology modules. The work also presents a range of examples illustrating the subtlety of this behavior. These examples demonstrate several distinct mechanisms by which local cohomology may fail to be tame, highlighting both the limitations of general tameness results and the complexity of the graded setting.
outputs.L4:
This work develops a duality theorem for a class of graded algebras and applies it to the study of local cohomology. The duality result provides a framework for relating graded components of local cohomology modules to appropriate dual or Ext-type constructions. In this way, it offers a systematic method for analyzing the asymptotic behavior of these modules and for determining when familiar finiteness or stability properties can be expected.

A central focus is the notion of tameness. A graded local cohomology module is typically called tame when its graded components eventually behave uniformly in sufficiently negative degrees: they are either all zero or all nonzero. Although such stability occurs under a number of standard hypotheses, the examples considered here show that it is not a general feature of graded local cohomology.

Through a varied collection of constructions, the work demonstrates several distinct forms of nontame behavior. In some cases, the negative graded components alternate between vanishing and nonvanishing; in others, their behavior follows more complicated or highly irregular patterns. These examples show that local cohomology can fail to stabilize even when the underlying graded algebra retains otherwise favorable structural properties.

Taken together, the duality theorem and the examples clarify both the possibilities and the limitations of general tameness results. They reveal that the asymptotic structure of graded local cohomology is considerably more subtle than might be suggested by well-behaved special cases, and they underscore the need for additional hypotheses in any theorem asserting eventual vanishing or nonvanishing.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a concise abstract for a mathematics article about duality in graded algebras and failures of tameness in local cohomology.
counterfactuals.output: We study duality phenomena in graded algebras and their interaction with local cohomology. Using graded Matlis duality and canonical modules, we establish criteria relating homological properties of a graded algebra to the structure of its local cohomology modules. We then construct examples showing that standard finiteness and tameness expectations may fail: graded components can exhibit irregular nonvanishing patterns, even under favorable Noetherian hypotheses. These results clarify the limits of duality-based control and identify conditions under which asymptotic tameness is recovered.

counterfactuals.output: The paper establishes a duality theorem for a class of graded algebras satisfying suitable finiteness and homological conditions. It constructs a dual algebra—typically through a graded dual, Ext-algebra, or Koszul-type construction—and proves that the derived categories of graded modules over the two algebras are equivalent. Under stronger hypotheses, applying the duality twice recovers the original algebra. The result unifies several familiar forms of graded and Koszul duality and provides tools for translating algebraic invariants, resolutions, and homological properties between the paired algebras.
